aria: Animated recap of the Nuggets' 151 to 145 overtime win at the Bulls: Jamal Murray's 27-foot 3-pointer with 4:41 left in overtime that broke a 131 to 131 tie, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Murray's 45 points, the top scorers, how the Nuggets won, and the next game.
notes: Box score from the Nuggets' 151–145 overtime win at the Chicago Bulls on Nov 22, 2026, from the Covers box score, checked line for line against the StatMuse game page. All 151 Denver points and all 145 Chicago points add up from the player lines. The quarter scores (33–39–33–26, OT 20, to 31–39–25–36, OT 14) add up to both totals: Denver led 72–70 at the half (Field Level Media; Denver Stiffs) and 105–95 after three (Denver Stiffs), and it was 131–131 after regulation. Points in the paint (66–48), second-chance points (25–11) and both biggest leads (Denver 12, Chicago 6) are from Covers and StatMuse; Field Level Media also gives 66–48 and 25–11. Threes (17 of 35 to 25 of 55), free throws (26 of 30 to 16 of 20), offensive rebounds (15–9) and assists (33–39) are from both box scores. Chicago's 25 threes matched the franchise record (Field Level Media; Roundtable via Yahoo). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Late in regulation (StatMuse play-by-play; Field Level Media; Roundtable via Yahoo): Aaron Gordon's tip dunk with 1:48 left put Denver ahead 126–124, Murray's 8-foot fadeaway and free throw with 40 seconds left made it 131–126, Josh Giddey answered with a three-point play with 27 seconds left (131–129), and Giddey's layup after a Jalen Smith steal tied it 131–131 with 2.1 seconds left (Field Level Media; StatMuse shows 0:02). Nikola Jokić missed a turnaround 3 at the horn (Field Level Media). Denver scored the first eight points of overtime (Roundtable; StatMuse: 134–131, 136–131, 139–131). Murray had six points in overtime (Field Level Media; StatMuse). Josh Giddey's 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists are from both box scores. Denver has won three straight, and five of six (Field Level Media). Chicago was without Norman Powell and Nic Claxton (Field Level Media).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jamal Murray's 3-pointer with 4:41 left in overtime, logged on the StatMuse play-by-play as a 27-foot step-back three assisted by Nikola Jokić, which turned 131–131 into 134–131. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc; the step-back footwork and the exact spot on the floor are not drawn. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Denver Nuggets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Murray's listed 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds with No. 27 (RealGM), with his arms scaled to a reported 6-foot-7 wingspan (CraftedNBA), in Denver's road kit. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
